newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian metals steady on low demand, limited supply.
newsitem.headline: Indian metals steady on low demand, limited supply.

text.p: Base metals were steady on the local market on Thursday, dealers said, on low indsutrial demand and limited supplies.
The transfer of imported metals from the Bombay port to markets was at low ebb on account of the strike by transport operators from April 1 onwards.

"Transport operators have gone on a nationwide strike to protest against imposition of service tax and hike in the insurance premium," said Sharad Parikh, the president of the Bombay Metal Exchange. "Our exchange has announced its support to the strike."
He added: "The Bombay metal market will be closed on Saturday for one day to show our support."
Copper was steady at 13,550 rupees per quintal as was zinc at 7,850 rupees and lead at 4,550 rupees per quintal.
"Aluminium was available at the previous level of 7,450 rupees per quintal but the undercurrent was firm on reports that some major Indian producers face shortage of ready stock," one broker said.
Tin was quiet at 31,600 rupees and nickel at 36,800 rupees per quintal.
